3	  "category": "architecture",
4	  "hypothesis": "Experiment 4 closed the exposure/sharpness route and the model did exactly what its architecture permits: it got much worse on its OWN training photographs (train_capture_diagnostics 0.060 / 0.053 / 0.088 -> 0.733 / 0.673 / 0.518, usable 94-96% -> 36-54%) while the held-out 2024 photograph improved only to 1.271 (usable 11.8%, false fix 38.8%), with training loss still falling steeply at epoch 8 (4.08, augmented top1 0.45 vs 0.79 before). The pre-registered hope was that capacity would 'move to the layout structure at 2 m scale and up that all four surveys share'. It cannot, because the trunk cannot see layout. Measured at design time on the current model (runs/_probe_exp5_rf.py, no training): the feature extractor is four 3x3 stride-2 convs, so each of the 8x8 = 64 positions of its final map has a receptive field of 31 x 31 px, i.e. 31 m of a 128 m frame, and global average pooling then averages those 64 local descriptors. The 160-d vector the 2,970-way classifier reads is therefore, by construction, a BAG OF 31 m TEXTURE PATCHES with all relative arrangement discarded: it can encode 'how much roof, asphalt, canopy, water of which tint and grain', but not 'a canal bends past a block of three courtyards with a wide road to the north'. The first is exactly what differs between a summer DOP20, a leaf-off 2022 and an early-spring 2023 survey (and what experiment 4 now randomises away); the second is what all four surveys share. With texture statistics randomised and arrangement unrepresentable, the model is left fitting whatever colour-and-grain statistics survive the augmentation, which is why it now underfits even its training photographs and why its mean_max_softmax is only 0.19. This is the one inference stage no experiment in this era has questioned: arch_json for experiments 2-4 carries changed:true only on 'Training signal' (and experiment 3's feature-consistency term), never on 'Feature extractor', and the trunk itself is byte-for-byte the mission-era one (chans [3,32,64,128,160], unchanged since commit 92d1f12). Extending the pyramid by two more stride-2 stages (8x8 -> 4x4 -> 2x2) takes the receptive field to 127 px, so every descriptor the pooling averages sees the whole frame and can represent arrangement; the two stages are depthwise-separable so they cost 55k parameters (+221 kB, 3.30 MB exported, under the 4 MiB gate) and negligible compute at 4x4 and 2x2 resolution. The earlier-era record contains 'tripled trunk depth made things worse' (four-area era experiments 26/28, pretrained MobileNetV3 on never-seen ground under a median metric) - that verdict is void here and asked a different question; this is a from-scratch trunk on fully-mapped ground, and the change is to receptive field, not to parameter count. Rotation remains the only geometric augmentation, so the pooled whole-frame descriptor still has to be learned rotation-invariant, as the texture one was.",
5	  "method": "ONE change, in model/model.py's CellLocNet.__init__: after the existing four standard 3x3 stride-2 conv+BN+ReLU stages (3->32->64->128->160, spatial 128->8, untouched), append two depthwise-separable stride-2 blocks, each = depthwise 3x3 stride-2 pad-1 conv (groups=160, no bias) + BN + ReLU + pointwise 1x1 conv 160->160 (no bias) + BN + ReLU, taking the map 8x8 -> 4x4 -> 2x2 and the receptive field 31 -> 63 -> 127 px. Global average pooling (now over 2x2), the 2,970-way cell head, the offset head, the 3x3 belief-pooling decode, confidence, loss, targets, the paired three-survey batches, nuisance augmentation, schedule, epochs and views per epoch are all untouched. Exported ONNX grows from 3,079,093 to ~3.30 MB.",
6	  "expected_outcome": "Mechanical check that must hold or the mechanism did not bite: training loss at epoch 8 falls well below experiment 4's 4.08 (predicted 2.8-3.4) and augmented train top1 rises from 0.45 to above 0.60, i.e. the model can now fit the augmented task it could not fit before. train_capture_diagnostics (bb_dop20 / truedop_2022 / truedop_2023 = 0.733 / 0.673 / 0.518 on experiment 4) are predicted to recover to 0.15-0.35 each, with coverage on them rising from 0.44-0.59 toward 0.8+. Primary (held-out truedop_2024): 1.271 -> predicted 0.95-1.15, with usable rising from 11.8% to 20-35% and false fix falling from 38.8% to 25-35%, because a layout descriptor that survives the augmentation is also one that a fourth survey of the same streets reproduces; median error on 2024 (1,911 m) should drop below 500 m as predictions stop collapsing onto look-alike texture cells. Decision rules: (a) training diagnostics recover AND 2024 improves -> supported; the feature now carries layout, and the next experiment can make that layout survey-invariant explicitly (experiment 3's cross-survey consistency redone on batch-centred features, which was vacuous on the old non-negative GAP texture vector) or add +-12 px jitter. (b) training diagnostics recover (0.15-0.35) but 2024 stays >= 1.2 -> the wide-receptive-field trunk memorised three survey-specific layouts-of-texture; the next move is cross-survey feature consistency or DINOv2 distillation, not more capacity. (c) training diagnostics do NOT recover (stay > 0.5) -> receptive field was not the binding limit; the 8-epoch budget under augmentation is, and the next experiment addresses optimisation (schedule / head capacity), not the trunk. Standing check: the score must move through usable_fix_rate and false_fix_rate, with 2024 coverage staying >= 0.2 (currently 0.505); model bytes must read ~3.30 MB and latency stays far under 250 ms.",
7	  "init_strategy": "from-scratch",
8	  "eli5": "Until now the model looked at each 128-metre-wide aerial frame through 64 small 31-metre peepholes and then averaged what it saw, so all it could remember about a place was its mix of textures and colours: so much roof, so much asphalt, so much tree, in these tints. That is exactly the stuff that changes between two photographs of the same streets taken in different seasons, and the previous experiment deliberately scrambled it, which left the model with almost nothing to hold on to. This experiment widens its view to the whole frame at once, so it can finally see how the roads, blocks and water are arranged relative to each other, which is the same in every photograph of Berlin ever taken. The extra two layers are cheap and the exported model still fits the drone's memory.",
9	  "architecture": {
10	    "stages": [
11	      {"name": "Camera frame", "detail": "128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw", "changed": false},
12	      {"name": "Feature extractor", "detail": "CHANGED: the four-stage strided conv stack (each output position saw only a 31 m window, then averaged — a bag of local textures) gains two cheap depthwise-separable stride-2 stages, so every pooled descriptor now sees the whole 128 m frame and can encode how roads, blocks and water are arranged, not just which textures are present (still 160 channels, +55k parameters)", "changed": true},
13	      {"name": "Map-cell classifier", "detail": "scores all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin and picks the tile this view belongs to — localization as multiple choice, not coordinate guessing", "changed": false},
14	      {"name": "Local belief pooling", "detail": "gathers the belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre", "changed": false},
15	      {"name": "Within-cell offset", "detail": "small head that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot", "changed": false},
16	      {"name": "Confidence gate", "detail": "confidence = the belief mass on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — a vote split across adjacent tiles still counts as knowing where you are; belief scattered across distant tiles still reads as unsure and the drone abstains", "changed": false},
17	      {"name": "Training signal", "detail": "unchanged from experiment 4: every training view is re-photographed at random (brightness, contrast, gamma, colour balance, saturation, blur, sensor grain) and each batch holds the same places in all three survey photographs; bilinear tile targets, residual offset target, cosine schedule, views per epoch unchanged", "changed": false, "train_only": true}
18	    ]
19	  },
20	  "implementation_brief": "Edit model/model.py; make one small logging addition to model/train.py. Nothing else changes.

model/model.py, class CellLocNet.__init__ — the trunk. Current code:
    chans = [3, 32, 64, 128, 160]
    layers = []
    for cin, cout in zip(chans, chans[1:]):
        layers += [nn.Conv2d(cin, cout, 3, stride=2, padding=1),
                   nn.BatchNorm2d(cout), nn.ReLU(inplace=True)]
    self.features = nn.Sequential(*layers)
Keep those four stages exactly as they are (same channels, same kernel/stride/padding, bias on, so the first four stages are byte-identical in shape to experiment 4). Immediately after the loop and BEFORE `self.features = nn.Sequential(*layers)`, append two depthwise-separable stride-2 blocks:
    c = chans[-1]  # 160
    for _ in range(2):
        layers += [nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, stride=2, padding=1, groups=c, bias=False),
                   nn.BatchNorm2d(c), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
                   nn.Conv2d(c, c, 1, bias=False),
                   nn.BatchNorm2d(c), nn.ReLU(inplace=True)]
Spatial map becomes 128 -> 64 -> 32 -> 16 -> 8 -> 4 -> 2; receptive field 31 -> 63 -> 127 px. Add a short comment stating the receptive-field purpose (whole-frame layout, not a 31 px texture window). The parameter count of the new blocks is 55,360 (verified at design time: runs/_probe_exp5_rf.py).

DO NOT change: training_outputs() (its `.mean(dim=(2, 3))` GAP now averages a 2x2 map — leave the code as is), forward() and the whole belief-pooling decode, cls_head / off_head (still Linear(160, n_cells) and Linear(160, 2)), CELL_PX, grid_dims, the cell_u/cell_v buffers, loss_fn, export_onnx (opset 17, dynamo=False; grouped conv exports fine), estimate_position. Update the module docstring's 'Current:' paragraph with one sentence: the trunk is four standard stride-2 convs plus two depthwise-separable stride-2 stages so the pooled feature's receptive field covers the whole 128 px frame.

model/train.py: ONLY add one key to the info dict returned by train_area, e.g. "trunk": "4 std 3x3 s2 convs [3,32,64,128,160] + 2 depthwise-separable 3x3 s2 blocks 160->160; RF 127 px; GAP over 2x2". Do not touch augment_views, AUG, extract_chunk, make_soft_targets, residual_offset_target, the training loop, the schedule, BATCH_SIZE, CHUNK_SIZE, logging, or load_scene (it reads only buckets(meta, 'train') — nothing under model/ may ever open the eval capture truedop_2024).

Contracts to preserve (the frozen scorer depends on them): train.py CLI exactly as now — `python -m model.train --area A --out-dir D [--data-dir P] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket M] [--seed S]`, writing train_info.json as a list of per-area dicts; ONNX export at <out>/models/<area>.onnx taking a 1x3x128x128 float32 input in [0,1] and returning [[u, v, conf]] with u, v normalised map coords and conf in [0,1], the whole decode inside the graph; exported size <= 4 MiB (expected ~3,300,000 bytes) and host latency <= 250 ms (expected a few ms).

Sanity before handing back (seconds, no training): build_model(json.load(open('data/berlin/meta.json'))), run forward on torch.zeros(1,3,128,128) and check output shape (1,3) with conf in [0,1]; check model.features(x).shape == (1,160,2,2); count parameters (expected ~812,000 total); export_onnx to a scratch path such as runs/_smoke_exp5/berlin.onnx, assert its size <= 4*1024*1024, load it with onnxruntime and run one inference to confirm the grouped convs export, then delete the scratch directory. Do not run training."

"""Technical architecture diagrams for experiments 1-6, drawn in tensor-native
visual language: images/fields as real grids, feature maps as 3D slabs,
vectors as tick-bars, FC as connection fans, decodes as lines converging to a
point. Captions sit under elements; no labeled boxes."""
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from autoresearch.db import connect
from terrain_frame_glyph import terrain_frame

INK, MUT, FAINT, ACC, OCH = "#111111", "#6b6a60", "#9b998c", "#8c2f1f", "#8a6a1e"
FONT = "Palatino,Georgia,serif"
IC = 112          # inference lane center y
LOSS_Y = 292      # loss-annotation row baseline


def txt(x, y, s, size=10, color=MUT, w=400, anchor="middle", style="", tid=None):
    tid_attr = f"id='{tid}' " if tid else ""
    return (f"<text {tid_attr}x='{x:.0f}' y='{y:.0f}' font-family='{FONT}' font-size='{size}' "
            f"fill='{color}' font-weight='{w}' text-anchor='{anchor}' {style}>{s}</text>")


def cap(xc, y, name, sub=None, color=MUT, name_color=None):
    out = [txt(xc, y, name, 10.5, name_color or (INK if color == MUT else color), 600)]
    if sub:
        out.append(txt(xc, y + 12, sub, 9.5, color))
    return "".join(out)


def harrow(x1, x2, y, label=None, color=FAINT):
    out = [f"<line x1='{x1}' y1='{y}' x2='{x2 - 5}' y2='{y}' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1'/>",
           f"<path d='M {x2},{y} l -6,-3 v 6 Z' fill='{color}'/>"]
    if label:
        out.append(txt((x1 + x2) / 2, y - 6, label, 9, FAINT, style="font-style='italic'"))
    return "".join(out)


def leader(x1, y1, x2, y2, color):
    """Slanted dashed annotation leader, paper-margin style."""
    return (f"<line x1='{x1}' y1='{y1}' x2='{x2}' y2='{y2}' stroke='{color}' "
            f"stroke-width='1' stroke-dasharray='2 4'/>")


def slab(x, s, d, color=INK):
    """Pseudo-3D feature-map slab: front s x s, depth d. Returns (svg, width)."""
    y = IC - s / 2
    dx, dy = d, d * 0.55
    out = [
        f"<polygon points='{x},{y} {x+dx},{y-dy} {x+dx+s},{y-dy} {x+s},{y}' "
        f"fill='#00000010' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1'/>",
        f"<polygon points='{x+s},{y} {x+dx+s},{y-dy} {x+dx+s},{y-dy+s} {x+s},{y+s}' "
        f"fill='#0000001c' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1'/>",
        f"<rect x='{x}' y='{y}' width='{s}' height='{s}' fill='#00000006' "
        f"stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1.2'/>",
    ]
    return "".join(out), s + dx


def imgsq(x, s, color=INK, tid=None):
    """Input image: square with a sparse pixel-grid texture."""
    y = IC - s / 2
    tid_attr = f"id='{tid}' " if tid else ""
    out = [f"<rect {tid_attr}x='{x}' y='{y}' width='{s}' height='{s}' fill='#00000008' "
           f"stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1.4'/>"]
    n = 6
    for i in range(1, n):
        out.append(f"<line x1='{x + i * s / n:.0f}' y1='{y}' x2='{x + i * s / n:.0f}' "
                   f"y2='{y + s}' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='0.4' opacity='0.3'/>")
        out.append(f"<line x1='{x}' y1='{y + i * s / n:.0f}' x2='{x + s}' "
                   f"y2='{y + i * s / n:.0f}' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='0.4' opacity='0.3'/>")
    for (a, b, o) in ((1, 2, .35), (3, 1, .5), (2, 4, .4), (4, 3, .3), (0, 4, .25), (4, 0, .3)):
        out.append(f"<rect x='{x + a * s / n:.0f}' y='{y + b * s / n:.0f}' "
                   f"width='{s / n:.0f}' height='{s / n:.0f}' fill='{color}' opacity='{o * 0.35}'/>")
    return "".join(out), s


def bar(x, h, color=INK, ticks=9):
    """1-D vector as a thin vertical tick-bar."""
    y = IC - h / 2
    out = [f"<rect x='{x}' y='{y}' width='7' height='{h}' fill='none' "
           f"stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1.2'/>"]
    for i in range(1, ticks):
        out.append(f"<line x1='{x}' y1='{y + i * h / ticks:.1f}' x2='{x + 7}' "
                   f"y2='{y + i * h / ticks:.1f}' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='0.5' opacity='0.5'/>")
    return "".join(out), 7


def fan(x1, h1, x2, h2, color=FAINT, n=5):
    """Fully-connected layer as a fan of crossing connections."""
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        ya = IC - h1 / 2 + (i + 0.5) * h1 / n
        for j in range(n):
            yb = IC - h2 / 2 + (j + 0.5) * h2 / n
            out.append(f"<line x1='{x1}' y1='{ya:.1f}' x2='{x2}' y2='{yb:.1f}' "
                       f"stroke='{color}' stroke-width='0.5' opacity='0.45'/>")
    return "".join(out)


def gridsq(x, s, n, color=INK, bumps=(), yc=None, lw=1.2):
    yc = IC if yc is None else yc
    y = yc - s / 2
    out = [f"<rect x='{x}' y='{y}' width='{s}' height='{s}' fill='none' "
           f"stroke='{color}' stroke-width='{lw}'/>"]
    for i in range(1, n):
        out.append(f"<line x1='{x + i * s / n:.1f}' y1='{y}' x2='{x + i * s / n:.1f}' "
                   f"y2='{y + s}' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='0.45' opacity='0.5'/>")
        out.append(f"<line x1='{x}' y1='{y + i * s / n:.1f}' x2='{x + s}' "
                   f"y2='{y + i * s / n:.1f}' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='0.45' opacity='0.5'/>")
    for (gx, gy, o) in bumps:
        out.append(f"<rect x='{x + gx * s / n:.1f}' y='{y + gy * s / n:.1f}' "
                   f"width='{s / n:.1f}' height='{s / n:.1f}' fill='{color}' fill-opacity='{o}'/>")
    return "".join(out), s


BUMP = ((5, 2, .55), (4, 2, .28), (5, 1, .28), (6, 2, .18), (5, 3, .18), (2, 5, .12), (1, 6, .1))


def crosspt(x, y, color, r=7):
    return (f"<line x1='{x - r}' y1='{y}' x2='{x + r}' y2='{y}' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1.4'/>"
            f"<line x1='{x}' y1='{y - r}' x2='{x}' y2='{y + r}' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1.4'/>"
            f"<circle cx='{x}' cy='{y}' r='{r * 0.55:.1f}' fill='none' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1.4'/>"
            f"<circle cx='{x}' cy='{y}' r='1.5' fill='{color}'/>")


def converge(gx, gs, tx, color, cells="all", n=8):
    """Decode drawn as cell-centers voting: lines from grid cells to a point."""
    out = []
    src = []
    y0 = IC - gs / 2
    if cells == "all":
        xs = ys = range(n)
    else:
        # 5x5 refinement window: cols 3-7, rows 1-5 — must match the red
        # window rect exp3 draws (wx = gx+3gs/8, wy = y0+1gs/8), so every
        # vote line starts at a cell center INSIDE the drawn window.
        xs, ys = range(3, 8), range(1, 6)
    for gyy in ys:
        for gxx in xs:
            if cells == "all" and (gxx + gyy) % 2:
                continue
            src.append((gx + (gxx + 0.5) * gs / n, y0 + (gyy + 0.5) * gs / n))
    for (sx, sy) in src:
        out.append(f"<line x1='{sx:.0f}' y1='{sy:.0f}' x2='{tx}' y2='{IC}' "
                   f"stroke='{color}' stroke-width='0.55' opacity='0.4'/>")
    out.append(crosspt(tx, IC, color))
    return "".join(out)


def gauge(x, yc, color=MUT, r=14):
    a = math.radians(55)
    return (f"<path d='M {x - r},{yc} A {r} {r} 0 0 1 {x + r},{yc}' fill='none' "
            f"stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1.2'/>"
            f"<line x1='{x}' y1='{yc}' x2='{x + (r - 3) * math.cos(a):.1f}' "
            f"y2='{yc - (r - 3) * math.sin(a):.1f}' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1.4'/>"
            f"<circle cx='{x}' cy='{yc}' r='1.6' fill='{color}'/>")


def lanes(h):
    return (txt(8, 26, "INFERENCE PATH — WHAT FLIES", 9, FAINT, 600, "start",
                "letter-spacing='1.8'")
            + txt(8, LOSS_Y - 34, "TRAINING SIGNALS — NEVER FLY", 9, OCH, 600, "start",
                  "letter-spacing='1.8'"))


def svgwrap(h, body):
    return (f"<svg viewBox='0 0 980 {h}' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' role='img'>"
            f"{body}</svg>")


def kernel_proj(x1, s1, x2, s2, color):
    """Conv connection: small kernel square on layer i's face, faint lines
    converging to a cell on layer i+1 — computed-from, not standing-next-to."""
    k = max(5, s1 * 0.30)
